title: 2020 AMC 12A Problem 3
statement: A driver travels for \(2\) hours at \(60\) miles per hour, during which her car gets \(30\) miles per gallon of gasoline. She is paid \(\$0.50\) per mile, and her only expense is gasoline at \(\$2.00\) per gallon. What is her net rate of pay, in dollars per hour, after this expense?

solutions.text:
In \(2\) hours she drives \(120\) miles, earning \(120 \cdot \$0.50 = \$60.\)

She uses \(120 \div 30 = 4\) gallons, costing \(4 \cdot \$2.00 = \$8.\)

Her net earnings are \(\$60 - \$8 = \$52,\) so her rate is \(\$52 \div 2 = \$26\) per hour.

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: In \(2\) hours she drives \(120\) miles; find her pay and her gasoline cost for that distance
Divide the net earnings by the \(2\) hours to get the rate per hour
